overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting insufficiently specific notices for its May 23 and June 21 meetings, but did not otherwise violate it; no intentional violation was found and no further remedial action was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 23 notice topics 'Update re: GU RR Request for Support of IRAP Grant' and 'Update re: 364 West Street' were insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the use of the acronyms “GU RR” and “IRAP” rendered the topic “Update re: GU RR Request for Support of IRAP Grant” insufficient to inform members of the public unfamiliar with this matter of the anticipated nature of the discussion.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the June 21 open session notice topic on the Special Town Meeting warrant gave no detail about the warrant article.
allegations.key_passage: We do, however, find a violation with respect to the open session topic where it did not include any detail regarding the warrant article to be discussed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the June 21 notice failed to identify the property or litigation in the executive session topic, which was the Purpose 3 and Purpose 6 basis for the closed session.
allegations.key_passage: However, in this instance because the Board’s entire executive session discussion properly fell under Purpose 3 such that the Board could have included the Purpose 3 notice topic alone, and because the Purpose 3 notice topic was sufficient, we find no violation with respect to notice of the Board’s June 21 executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the June 21 executive session was improper because the litigation was already stipulated dismissed and eminent domain involves no negotiation.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board properly met in executive session on June 21.

allegations.summary: Complainant's allegations about whether the Board properly voted to invite and retain Anderson & Kreiger and about a firm letter were declined as outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Where these allegations, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review them.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
